newsitem.title: FRANCE: INTERVIEW - Leclerc seeks growth abroad, partners.
newsitem.headline: INTERVIEW - Leclerc seeks growth abroad, partners.

text.p: French retailer Leclerc bought a 20 percent stake in Swiss central buying operation European Marketing Distribution (EMD) to expand abroad and possibly forge partnerships, co-chairman Michel-Edouard Leclerc said on Friday.
"We're looking for partners," he said. "If we find people within the network who share our philosophy and objectives, we wouldn't rule out their using Leclerc's name in their markets."
Privately-owned Leclerc groups 450 franchise-holders running 550 hypermarkets and supermarkets with annual sales of 130 billion francs ($24 billion). Leclerc has 16 percent of the French market.

EMD groups independent federations in more than 12 countries with more than 50,000 stores, with a combined turnover of 660 billion francs. It serves as a buyer and negotiator for its members, which include Germany's Markant and Norway's Unil A/L.
Leclerc bought its stake in EMD through Eurolec, a European buying company it had formed.

"Our objective in this deal with EMD is to participate in an organised distribution network, exploit synergies and know-how," Leclerc said. "We're looking for synergies to accelerate our development abroad, improve our product lines and services for our members."
He said the pressure was high because of restrictions in France on expanding floor space and opening new superstores.
The restrictions included in a law passed last year have spurred a consolidation in the French retail industry and prompted retailers to step up their development abroad.

"If we want to remain in the lead, we really need to break out of the isolation in which French regulations have left us in terms of price policies. What we're looking for now is European retailers which, like us, want to remain independent," he said.
But he said Leclerc, ranked second in France after privately owned Intermarche, was not under pressure to form an alliance rapidly as it had its own expansion plans.
In the next year and a half, it plans 17 projects in Portugal, Spain, Poland and possibly other countries, he said.
"In any case, with our turnover, we have exceeded the minimum critical mass," he said.
